data.gender_notes: Saathvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Saath', meaning truth, and 'Vika', meaning speaker. Saathvika represents a truth speaker or a person who speaks the truth. The name Saathvika carries the meaning “Truth Speaker” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saathvika usually hope their child will grow to embody truth speaker and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies truth and honesty.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saathvika total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Saathvika holds deep significance. Truth is considered a fundamental aspect of spiritual growth and enlightenment in Hinduism. Saathvika, being the truth speaker, represents one who seeks knowledge, wisdom, and self-realization by uncovering the truth within oneself. The name carries an inherent purity that fosters mental clarity, emotional balance, and spiritual growth. It reminds us of the importance of speaking the truth and striving for inner truth on our spiritual journey.

vedic_reference.note: The name Saathvika is derived from the Sanskrit language and is composed of two roots: Sattva (goodness) and Anushta (devoted) or Anugrahaarh (grace-giving). It signifies one who is devoted to the principles of goodness and bestows grace upon others.

historical_references.reference: Saathvika was the name of a famous courtesan from the Vijayanagara Empire in the late 16th century. She was renowned for her exceptional beauty and musical skills.
Saathvika was also the name of an influential figure in the 13th century Bhakti movement. She was a devotee of Lord Shiva and composed several hymns in his praise.
